column2: rule and its stated exception: PRD 151 makes an unknown option a usage error unless ignore-unknown-options is set; PRD 380 lists the usage-error class (exit 2) for the default case
scope: "unknown long options are left intact" (PRD 151) describes token handling under ignore-unknown-options, the case the same sentence opens with
rule and its stated exception: leaf commands may mix options and arguments (PRD 134); within a chaining group they are not mixed (PRD 310)
rule and its stated exception: leaf-command mixing (PRD 134); chained subcommands put options before arguments (PRD 310)
default and opt-in: group options before the subcommand name by default (PRD 221); an author may enable mixing on a group (PRD 134)
rule and its stated exception: options appear on the help page (PRD 23) unless hidden (PRD 112)
different properties: a custom listing decides which names exist (PRD 227); a name marked hidden is still left out of help and completion (PRD 421)
rule and its stated exception: parameters are passed to the function (PRD 84) unless hidden from the callback (PRD 146, expose_value)
one sentence, two token kinds: with extra arguments allowed, non-option-shaped leftovers are tolerated and option-shaped ones still need ignore-unknown-options or `--` (PRD 91)
two settings both needed: an option-shaped leftover needs ignore-unknown-options (PRD 91) and allowed extra arguments (PRD 151); neither alone suffices
scope: PRD 151's "leftover option-like tokens become extra arguments" is under "configured to ignore unknown options", the same condition PRD 91 names
rule and its stated exception in one paragraph: replaced help names print help; a name an author option reuses runs that option (PRD 113)
different flag kinds: PRD 142's conversion error is for plain boolean flags; "unrecognized values are unset" is for flags with a non-boolean flag-value
different flag kinds: whitespace-only deactivates a plain boolean flag; for a flag with a non-boolean flag-value an empty value is unset (PRD 142)
different cases: an optional argument gets its default (PRD 166); a missing required argument is a usage error (PRD 174)
different cases: an omitted optional argument gets its default (PRD 166); a value that fails conversion is a usage error (PRD 207)
different cases: group invoked with no subcommand does not run the group callback (PRD 118); group callback runs when a subcommand is dispatched (PRD 220)
different callbacks and cases: a missing required argument stops that command's callback (PRD 174); the group callback runs when a subcommand is dispatched (PRD 220)
different cases: group callback on dispatch (PRD 220); a file that cannot be opened stops the command callback (PRD 298)
different types: File delivers an open file (IC 215); Path delivers a path, path_type is a Path parameter (IC 216)
different callbacks: a refused value stops the command callback; parameter callbacks run for every value source (PRD 145)
different callbacks: the command callback does not run on a refusal; a missing parameter's own parameter callback still runs (PRD 145)
rule and its stated exception: a missing required option is a usage error (PRD 135, 145) unless a source supplies it; a prompt is such a source (PRD 269)
stated condition in one paragraph: a non-required prompting option uses its default when omitted; a required one prompts (PRD 269)
stated condition in one paragraph: non-required option uses the default when omitted; a required prompting option prompts (PRD 269)
different option kinds: a counting option yields 0 when omitted (PRD 137); prompting is only for options declared to prompt (PRD 269)
stated outright: a deprecated argument cannot be required, an argument with no default or optional marking is required, so that combination is refused at declaration (PRD 177)
different parameter kinds: a default-map string is split for per-occurrence arity other than one; for a one-value repeatable option it is refused (PRD 247)
different answers: n/no is a negative answer and returns false; "any other answer" means one that is neither yes nor no and asks again (PRD 271)
optional check and default: "must exist" is a selectable check; by default existence is not required (PRD 292)
scoped: permission checks apply only to a path that exists (PRD 292)
scoped: writability is not checked by default and permission checks apply only to an existing path (PRD 292)

an allowed dash means a standard stream, not a file: it is delivered as `-` without the file checks; only a disallowed dash is "an ordinary path ... when a file of that name satisfies the checks" (PRD 292)
optional check and default: executability is selectable and not checked by default (PRD 292)
rule and its stated exception: Unix uses the config home; POSIX-forced mode uses the home dot folder "regardless of XDG_CONFIG_HOME" (PRD 339)
scope: the config-home placement is stated "On Unix" (PRD 339); other platforms have their own location
default and mode: macOS default is Library/Application Support; the POSIX-forced mode is an explicit override on POSIX systems (PRD 339)
scope per platform: the lowercased dashed name is "On Unix"; macOS uses the name as given (PRD 339)
rule and its stated exception: platform config location by default; POSIX-forced mode overrides it (PRD 339)
default and opt-out: automatic help by default (PRD 113); a command may disable it (PRD 120)
default and opt-out: automatic help (PRD 39); a command may disable it (PRD 120)
different cases: an omitted optional option gets an absent value (PRD 131); an omitted required option is a usage error (PRD 135)
different option configurations: an optional-value option with an author flag-value (PRD 139); an option that prompts on a bare flag (PRD 269)
different components: the open helper opens stdin for `-` (PRD 286); the Path type delivers `-` without reading a stream (PRD 292)
different components: open helper (PRD 286) versus Path type with dash disallowed (PRD 292)
different components: the dash is not special for the Path type (PRD 292); the stdin/stdout rule is for the File type and the open helper (PRD 420)
different types: File delivers an open file (PRD 290); Path delivers a path (PRD 292)
different stages: command-line tokens are text (PRD 58); the File type converts the token into an open file (PRD 290)
rule and its stated case: naming a subcommand runs it (PRD 219); a nested group named with nothing after shows help without its callback, the no-arguments rule of the same PRD 219
different encodings: an author-declared file encoding (PRD 290); the environment's ASCII-only stream encoding that echo works around (PRD 330)
two accepted forms: a conversion function may refuse by ValueError (IC 129) or by BadParameter (IC 203)
stated in the same table: an omitted repeatable option is `()` (IC 174); `None` is for other omitted parameters (IC 175)
two modes: default capture does not record descriptor writes; file-descriptor capture does (PRD 405)
rule and its stated exception: single newlines are not hard breaks, except in a paragraph led by a backspace line (PRD 107)
rule and its stated exception: help text is rewrapped, except a backspace-led paragraph (PRD 107)

rule and stated exception: hidden prompts are not echoed (PRD 404, 280, no mode exception); the stdin-echo mode adds echoes of reads beyond prompt echoes. Reading kept: hidden input stays hidden in every mode
same as CF-000085: hidden input is never echoed into captured output (PRD 280); the stdin-echo mode does not lift that
different contexts: token normalization in parsing (PRD 250); suggestions for an incomplete token in completion (PRD 365)
different decorators: option nargs is a positive int (IC 136); argument nargs may be -1 for variadic (IC 163)
different option kinds: an on/off pair yields true/false (PRD 136); an optional-value option yields its flag-value or token (PRD 139)
default and override: styles kept on a terminal by autodetection; the invocation may force colour off (PRD 330)
no conflict: PRD 54 says it is intended to work on Linux, macOS and Windows and names Linux as the supported target; the hardware note says those hosts are sufficient to install and use it
different types: open-bound clamping is for integer ranges (PRD 196); float ranges allow clamp only with closed bounds (PRD 197)
word sense: "a sequence is used as-is" is a Python sequence value in the default map (PRD 247), not an ANSI escape sequence (PRD 331)
word sense: a default-map sequence value (PRD 247) is not a terminal key sequence (PRD 334)
rule and its stated exception: the bar shows progress on a terminal; an explicitly hidden bar prints nothing (PRD 333)
different values: an unrecognized completion instruction prints nothing (PRD 367); the source instruction prints the registration script (IC 309)
different keys: show_default on an option may be a string (IC 150); the context setting show_default is a bool (IC 240)
